primary_claim: An ordinary gradient-descent training setup with no deliberately obfuscated computation, just memorization of secret strings with hard negatives, is enough to implant secrets in deep MLPs that resist recovery by input-optimization attacks (the GCG-style battery gets approximately 0/16 on 3-layer organisms) and are only partially recovered by a trained weight-reading transformer (e.g. 1.82/16 at top-16 rising to 3.28/16 at top-1024 on 64-bit 3-layer organisms).

effect.metric: recovery (secrets found out of 16) via input-optimization battery vs trained weight-reader, hard-negative depth-3 organisms
effect.value: input-optimization battery ~0/16; weight-reader 1.82/16 (top-16) to 3.28/16 (top-1024) on 64-bit; 0.00-0.04/16 on 34-bit

stated_future_work: use this setup as a benchmark for more advanced interpretability methods
feed the secrets to the weight-reader along the model weights and make it predict which other (negative) inputs cause the model to produce a high logit
explore low probability estimation methods, which would require access to the training process
limitations_stated: the recovery metric doesn't consider false positives, though the authors don't think this is a major limitation
GCG is limited as eliciting bad contexts in LLMs usefully, as it produces unrealistic inputs and might not work in modern LLMs or for more specific behaviors
the 34-bit reader overfits: validation recovery peaks and then decays back toward 0 while train recovery keeps climbing
quote: So an ordinary training setup with no deliberately obfuscated computation, just memorization with hard negatives, is enough to implant secrets that resist detection by both human-made input-optimization algorithms and learned algorithms.
